a_qualified_scholar.heading: How to find a qualified scholar
steps: Ask in person. At a mosque or a place of learning you trust, ask who answers questions like yours, and take your question to that scholar with the details of your own situation.
A ruling on your own situation comes from a scholar who has heard it. No answer on this platform is one.
If it matters to you, ask the scholar what they studied and with whom.
a_qualified_scholar.names_none_because: This platform names no scholar and no body: it cannot check anyone's standing as a scholar, and which scholar to ask is for you and your community to choose.
a_qualified_scholar.this_platform: This platform is not a scholar and gives no religious ruling. What its AI composes on religion is withheld until a named scholar approves that exact text, and no scholar answers questions from the public here.

page.to_complain: To complain about an answer, raise a claim. Under the answer of each of the 25 domain tools on the Law, Care, Education, Employment, Science and Religion pages, say what is wrong and the claim is raised from there; against a saved deliverable, raise a claim on the support page. A claim about an answer carries the fingerprint of its text and what served it, never the text itself. A claim is filed as a change that only a person decides, and it stays open until a person answers it; with sign-in off, the Owner answers every claim. This platform is not a regulated provider, so no ombudsman or regulator handles complaints about it.
